_note: Scripted replies for the mock provider, so the agent loop can be demonstrated with no model, no key and no network. Two entries return a broken first answer and a fixed second one, which is what makes the --ablate run show a non-zero recovery. These are canned responses, NOT model output: a real accuracy number needs --provider anthropic or --provider ollama.
GPA above 3.5: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM students s WHERE s.gpa > 3.5
names of students in Computer Sciences: SELECT students.name FROM departments JOIN students ON departments.id = students.dept_id WHERE departments.name = 'Computer Sciences'
at least one student enrolled: SELECT c.title FROM courses c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e WHERE e.course_id = c.id)
years 2 through 3: SELECT name FROM students WHERE year BETWEEN 2 AND 3
each instructor with their department: SELECT i.name, d.name FROM instructors i, departments d WHERE i.dept_id = d.id
year 1 or later: SELECT name FROM students WHERE gpa > 3.0 AND dept_id = 1
average instructor salary: SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) FROM instructors GROUP BY dept_id
by GPA, highest first: SELECT name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa IS NOT NULL ORDER BY gpa DESC
titles of Computer Sciences courses: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE dept_id = 1
each student with their department: SELECT s.name, d.name FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.dept_id = d.id
